extracted.intended_audience: undergraduates, graduate students, postdocs, and early-career mathematicians seeking academic career advice
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of practical, stage-by-stage career and research guidelines for people pursuing academic careers in mathematics (undergraduate → graduate → postdoc and early career). Emphasises habits, attitude, learning, presentation, and time management.

rubrics_metrics.name: How can one become better at solving mathematical problems?
rubrics_metrics.description: How can one become better at solving mathematical problems?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as an undergraduate-level concern; the page links to a separate discussion on improving problem-solving skills (implicit advice: practice problem solving, study techniques specific to problem solving).

rubrics_metrics.name: More to maths than grades and exams and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that there is more to maths than grades and exams and methods; there is also more to maths than rigour and proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages valuing broader mathematical thinking and understanding beyond formal correctness and test performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value partial progress
rubrics_metrics.description: It is also important to value partial progress, as a crucial stepping stone to a complete solution of a problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat partial results and incremental advances as meaningful contributions and learning steps rather than failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't base career decisions on glamour or fame
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t base career decisions on glamour or fame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose paths based on substantive fit and opportunities rather than perceived prestige.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study at different places
rubrics_metrics.description: But you should study at different places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gain diverse training and perspectives by studying at more than one institution when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss career decisions with your advisor
rubrics_metrics.description: I would in particular recommend discussing such decisions with your advisor if you have one, as he or she will be familiar with your situation and will likely be able to provide pertinent advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use advisors as informed, context-aware sounding boards when making important career choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work hard and work professionally; enjoy your work
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important to work hard, and work professionally. But it is also important to enjoy your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance diligence and professionalism with maintaining intrinsic enjoyment and motivation for sustained success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think ahead and ask ‘dumb’ questions to clarify direction
rubrics_metrics.description: Think ahead to understand the way forward; ask yourself dumb questions to understand the way before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan research directions and use simple/naïve questions to expose assumptions and clarify the path forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend talks and conferences broadly
rubrics_metrics.description: Attend talks and conferences, even those not directly related to your own work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expose yourself to diverse ideas and communities; serendipitous connections often arise from attending broader events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talk to your advisor but take initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: Talk to your advisor, but also take the initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain communication with mentors while proactively driving your own research and career decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid premature obsession with a single big problem or theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t prematurely obsess on a single “big problem” or “big theory”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep options open early in your career; avoid investing all effort in a single high-risk direction before other foundations are built.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write down what you've done and make your work available
rubrics_metrics.description: Write down what you’ve done, and make your work available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clear records of progress and disseminate results (preprints, notes, papers); see linked advice on how to write and submit papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn and relearn your field; learn outside your field too
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn and relearn your field, but don’t be afraid to learn things outside your field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuously update core knowledge while branching into other areas to gain complementary tools and perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn limitations of your tools and power of others' tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn the limitations of your tools, but also learn the power of other mathematician’s tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be self-aware about which techniques suit which problems, and study other approaches to expand your toolkit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim just beyond your current range
rubrics_metrics.description: In particular, you should continually aim just beyond your current range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue problems that stretch your abilities but are realistically attainable to foster steady growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be flexible and patient in research
rubrics_metrics.description: In your research, be both flexible and patient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt to new information and be willing to change approaches; allow time for ideas to mature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel, present research, and tailor talks to audience
rubrics_metrics.description: You should definitely travel and present your research if given the opportunity. But be considerate of your audience; talks are not the same as papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take opportunities to present widely; prepare talks differently from written papers and be audience-aware.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be sceptical of your own work; use the wastebasket
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sceptical of your own work, and don’t be afraid to use the wastebasket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically evaluate and discard ideas that do not hold up instead of clinging to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Batch low-intensity tasks to reduce distraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Batch low-intensity tasks together to take advantage of economies of scale and to reduce distraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group routine/administrative tasks into blocks so deep research work is less interrupted and more productive.
